Home / Museum Ship Reports / Ex-US Battleship Guns, Bora Bora

Location: Bora Bora, French Polynesia

Visited: 30 December 2022

The USS Connecticut (BB-18) was a pre-dreadnought battleship completed in 1906 and sold for scrap in 1923 under the terms of the Washington Naval Treaty. But her guns were kept in storage, and in 1942, eight of the 7-inch guns were mounted in four two-gun batteries on the island of Bora Bora in French Polynesia, to protect the fuelling depot that the USN was developing there:

  • Faanui (North Battery): Positioned to overlook the northern approaches.
  • Anau Fort (East Battery): Placed at Point Tuahora to watch the eastern side of the island.
  • Matira (South Battery): Situated near Point Matira to cover the southern lagoon access.
  • Cannoni Americani (West Battery): Located near Povai Bay/Point Tereia to protect the western anchorage.

In 2022 I had the opportunity to inspect all four battery sites. Seven of the guns are still mounted in their original positions, with just the carriage left from the missing eighth gun.

The guns are still reasonably intact, and constitute an ongoing memorial to both the USS Connecticut, and the US servicemen who were based in Bora Bora from 1942-46.
